on public perceptions of individuals with criminal records.", "quotes": [{"text": "The more negative angle for campaign advertisements and rhetoric is important to note: prior evidence on the effects of negative campaign advertisements suggests that they tend to be utilized less by those leading in the polls [4,5] and that Democrats tend to respond more to positive ads, compared to Republicans of his ability to win the presidential election (e.g., encouraging action and anger towards Trump), social categorization theory [12–15] would suggest that the effects of utilizing this label likely spilled over.", "page": 2}, {"text": "The extent to which individuals feel angry towards those with criminal records has been found to be associated with greater support for more punitive justice system policy [11].", "page": 2}]}, "central_claim": [{"claim": "Exposure to a political advertisement labeling Donald Trump as a 'convicted criminal' significantly decreases Democrats' positive
